title: Anaemia in pregnancy: Anaemia Mukt Bharat protocol
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Antenatal clinic, PHC to district hospital (FRU), labour room
summary: Anaemia in pregnancy is Hb below 11 g/dL (below 10.5 in the second trimester, WHO 2024). Give daily IFA from the second trimester; treat mild or moderate anaemia with 2 IFA tablets daily; IV iron after the first trimester if oral iron fails or Hb is 5 to 6.9 g/dL up to 34 weeks; transfuse if Hb is below 5 or severe after 34 weeks.

sections.title: Define and grade
items: Anaemia in pregnancy (Anaemia Mukt Bharat, AMB): Hb below 11.0 g/dL. Mild 10.0 to 10.9, moderate 7.0 to 9.9, severe below 7.0 g/dL.
WHO 2024 cut-offs: below 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters and below 10.5 g/dL in the second trimester (second trimester mild 9.5 to 10.4, moderate 7.0 to 9.4, severe below 7.0 g/dL).
Measure Hb by full blood count where available, otherwise a digital haemoglobinometer; do not use the haemoglobin colour scale.
Warning signs of decompensation at any Hb: breathlessness at rest, tachycardia, oedema, signs of heart failure. These need admission.

Iron deficiency is the commonest cause; also consider folate or B12 deficiency, hookworm, malaria, haemoglobinopathy (thalassaemia trait, sickle cell disease, common in some tribal and central Indian populations), chronic infection and blood loss.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CBC with red cell indices and peripheral smear; serum ferritin where available (low ferritin confirms iron deficiency; inflammation can raise it).
Microcytosis not responding to iron, or normal ferritin: haemoglobin HPLC or electrophoresis for thalassaemia or sickle cell, and test the partner if a trait is found.
Stool for ova (hookworm), malaria test in endemic areas or with fever, urine examination; B12 and folate if macrocytic.
Recheck Hb 1 month after starting treatment to confirm response.

sections.title: Prophylaxis for every pregnant woman (AMB)
items: Folic acid 400 mcg daily from before conception through the first trimester.
One IFA tablet (60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) daily from the fourth month (second trimester), for at least 180 days in pregnancy, and one daily for 180 days after birth.
Albendazole 400 mg as a single dose after the first trimester, preferably in the second trimester.

Take IFA with vitamin C rich foods (amla, guava, citrus); separate it from tea, coffee and calcium tablets. Encourage iron-rich foods: green leafy vegetables, whole pulses, millets such as ragi and bajra, and meat, fish or eggs where eaten.

sections.title: Mild and moderate anaemia (Hb 7.0 to 10.9 g/dL)
items: Two IFA tablets daily (120 mg elemental iron + 1 mg folic acid) if taking oral iron is feasible, and recheck Hb after 1 month.
Hb risen by 1 g/dL or more: continue 2 tablets daily, recheck at 2 months, and return to the prophylactic dose once Hb is 11 g/dL or more.
Rise below 1 g/dL after 1 month, intolerance or non-adherence (after the first trimester): refer to the FRU or district hospital for IV iron and look for another cause.
Anaemia first detected after 34 weeks: refer to the FRU or district hospital, because there is little time for oral iron to work before birth.

sections.title: IV iron (second and third trimester, and postpartum)
items: Indications (AMB): moderate anaemia after the first trimester or postpartum when oral iron is not tolerated or not taken, or Hb rises less than 1 g/dL after 1 month of oral IFA; severe anaemia (Hb 5.0 to 6.9 g/dL) at 13 to 34 weeks. WHO 2025 also supports IV iron when rapid correction is needed, if anaphylaxis can be managed.
Total iron deficit (Ganzoni): pre-pregnancy weight in kg x (target Hb 11 minus actual Hb in g/dL) x 2.4, plus 500 mg for stores (15 mg/kg if weight below 35 kg).

Iron sucrose: 200 mg in 100 mL 0.9% saline over 20 to 30 minutes, starting slowly for the first 5 minutes; maximum 600 mg per week (3 doses of 200 mg). Expected Hb rise at 3 weeks is about 1.6 g/dL in moderate and 2.5 g/dL in severe anaemia.
Ferric carboxymaltose: up to 20 mg/kg per infusion, maximum 1000 mg per infusion and per week, diluted in 0.9% saline (up to 250 mL) over at least 15 minutes; allows total dose in 1 or 2 visits.

Do not give in the first trimester, with iron overload, anaemia not due to iron deficiency (thalassaemia, sickle cell, haemolysis), known iron hypersensitivity, liver disease, renal failure or acute heart failure.

Give at PHC level or above under a medical officer with resuscitation equipment ready. Check BP, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature and fetal heart before, every 5 minutes during, and at the end; confirm cannula patency first (extravasation stains skin). Stop at any reaction; treat anaphylaxis with IM adrenaline.

sections.title: Severe anaemia and transfusion
items: Hb below 7 g/dL: refer urgently to the FRU or district hospital.
Hb 5.0 to 6.9 g/dL at 34 weeks or less: IV iron (iron sucrose or FCM) at the FRU or district hospital.
Hb 5.0 to 6.9 g/dL after 34 weeks: admit and transfuse.
Hb below 5 g/dL at any gestation: admit immediately for blood transfusion.
Transfuse packed red cells one unit at a time with reassessment, watching for circulatory overload; women with heart failure need HDU care.
Anaemic women in labour: IV access, group and crossmatch, active management of the third stage, and a low threshold to treat PPH, because they tolerate blood loss poorly.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: IV iron in the first trimester, or for anaemia due to thalassaemia or sickle cell disease.
Not rechecking Hb after 1 month, so ineffective oral iron continues until term.
Transfusing a stable woman with moderate anaemia early in pregnancy instead of giving iron.
Fast transfusion in severe chronic anaemia causing pulmonary oedema.
Missing malaria, hookworm or a haemoglobinopathy; stopping IFA at delivery instead of continuing for 180 days postpartum.

drugs.name: IFA tablet (60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid)
drugs.dose: Prophylaxis: 1 tablet daily from the second trimester for at least 180 days, and 180 days postpartum. Treatment: 2 tablets daily
drugs.notes: Red sugar-coated tablet supplied under Anaemia Mukt Bharat. Constipation and nausea common; take after food if needed.

drugs.name: Folic acid
drugs.dose: 400 mcg orally daily from preconception to the end of the first trimester

drugs.name: Albendazole
drugs.dose: 400 mg orally, single dose after the first trimester

drugs.name: Iron sucrose
drugs.dose: 200 mg in 100 mL 0.9% saline IV over 20 to 30 minutes; maximum 600 mg per week
drugs.notes: Total dose by Ganzoni formula. After the first trimester only. Monitor during infusion.

drugs.name: Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM)
drugs.dose: Up to 20 mg/kg (maximum 1000 mg) IV in up to 250 mL 0.9% saline over at least 15 minutes; maximum 1000 mg per week
drugs.notes: Second and third trimester and postpartum. Monitor during infusion; resuscitation equipment ready.

drugs.name: Packed red cells
drugs.dose: One unit at a time, reassessing between units
drugs.notes: Hb below 5 g/dL at any gestation, or 5.0 to 6.9 g/dL after 34 weeks, or decompensation.
